observations: Photo 0: Hand holding a black Nikon DSLR camera with lens cap on and strap attached, indoors.
Photo 1: Front view of the same camera with lens cap on; 'Nikon' visible on the lens barrel and camera body.
Photo 2: Rear view showing the LCD screen, control buttons, and 'Nikon' logo below the screen; strap attached.

claims.evidence: Nikon brand is readable in photos 0-2, but the D60 model number is not visible in any photo.
A lens is present in photos 0-1, but the lens model is not readable.
Camera function cannot be tested from still photos.

risks.risk: Camera may not power on or function (shutter, sensor, controls)
risks.proof: Video of the camera turning on, taking a photo, and displaying the image on the LCD.

risks.risk: Lens may have fungus, scratches, or focus/aperture problems
risks.proof: Close-up photos of front and rear lens glass, plus a sample photo taken through the lens.
risks.if_unproven: as faulty lens or body only

risks.risk: Shutter count may be high or unknown
risks.proof: Screenshot of shutter count or an unedited photo with readable EXIF data.

risks.risk: Battery, charger, or memory card may be missing
risks.proof: Photo of the battery, charger, and any memory card included.

proof_requests: Video showing the camera powering on, taking a photo, and reviewing it on the LCD
Close-up photos of the lens front and rear glass
Photo of the battery, charger, and any memory card
Screenshot of shutter count or original photo with EXIF data
response.reason: The item is identifiable as a Nikon DSLR camera from the photos, so it can be priced at its worst case as non-working pending proof of function.
